goals: Make the agent discoverable by other agents and explorers
Advertise MCP, A2A and web endpoints in one place
Keep the payee address correct after key changes

Tutorials written before 2026-01-25 still use endpoints and score
The agentId is known only after minting, so the file must be published twice

register and setAgentURI calls, or an SDK such as agent0-sdk

The registry owner not to upgrade the contracts against them
Explorers to read the file the same way they do

Register a test agent on Ethereum Sepolia or Base Sepolia

Time to rebind the wallet after a change
personas.story: Ana ships a weather agent with an MCP server. She writes a registration file, pins it to IPFS and calls register on Base Sepolia. The Registered event gives her agent id 812, so she adds it to the registrations list, pins the new file and calls setAgentURI. Her MCP server lives on another domain, so she serves the well-known file there too. An old tutorial told her to add an agentWallet endpoint; she deletes it and asks her payment wallet to sign the AgentWalletSet message instead, within the five-minute window. Before mainnet she checks that explorers show her services and the x402Support flag.

Leave feedback that others can verify

The payment rail it uses, such as x402

firstSteps: Resolve the agent file and check its registrations entry
Call getSummary with reviewers it trusts
metrics: Spend on agents without trusted feedback
personas.story: A research agent needs a translation service. It queries an indexer for agents tagged with translation skills, reads each registration file and drops those whose MCP endpoint does not answer. For the rest it calls getSummary with the twenty client addresses its operator trusts. It pays the best one through x402 at the address returned by getAgentWallet, keeps the transaction hash, uploads a feedback file with proofOfPayment and then calls giveFeedback with the file URI. The gas comes from a sponsor, as the text allows for clients that need not be registered.

The registry code, which one key can upgrade

Can I lower a response after a pass, and should I?
firstSteps: Read the Validation Registry section and issue 28
Deploy the reference contract on a local chain
personas.story: Kai runs a TEE attestation service and wants to post results through ERC-8004. He finds the Validation Registry in the text, but the contracts README lists no address and calls that part still under discussion. A contract answers at the scripted address on Base, yet nobody announced it, so he does not build on it. He deploys the reference code on a local chain instead, posts a soft response and then a hard one, and notices that a later answer can also lower a pass. He follows the open issue on that and waits for an official deployment.

personas.role: Sells an API or agent service, registers it so buyers can find it, and receives payments at agentWallet.
pains: Competitors and spammers can rate it from fresh addresses
Responses do not change a low score
x402 payments look like ordinary transfers to indexers
implements: x402Support true and an agentWallet bound by signature
appendResponse to answer complaints, for example with refund evidence
revenues feedback through its facilitator, as best practices suggest
mustTrust: The facilitator that publishes revenues feedback
questions: How do I get feedback from real customers counted?
What happens to my reputation if I sell the agent token?
firstSteps: Register the service with x402Support true
Ask paying clients to include proofOfPayment
personas.story: Omar sells a pricing API to agents and already takes x402 payments. He registers it with x402Support true and binds a cold wallet as agentWallet. A week later a burst of zero scores arrives from addresses that never paid him. He cannot delete them, so he appends responses that link to his payment logs and asks his facilitator to publish revenues feedback, as the best-practices guide suggests. His larger buyers already pass a trusted reviewer list to getSummary, and the burst never shows up in their numbers.

firstSteps: Index the identity and reputation events for the chains you use
Alert on transfers and wallet changes
personas.story: Lena runs controls for a company whose agents buy data from other agents. She indexes Transfer, URIUpdated and MetadataSet events and refuses payment to any agent whose token moved since its wallet was last bound. She scores reputation only from reviewers that paid with a verifiable proofOfPayment. Spending caps live in her payment layer, because ERC-8004 has none. When she learns that one externally owned account can upgrade the registries, she adds an alert on the proxy implementation slot and writes the risk into her vendor review.

personas.role: Studies the registries, the deployed proxies and the feedback data for attacks and failure modes.
goals: Measure Sybil feedback and placeholder registrations
pains: No public log query over large block ranges on free RPCs
implements: eth_call reads of owner and implementation slots
mustTrust: The census and study methods it reuses
questions: How much feedback is grounded in payment?
firstSteps: Read the Security Considerations and PR 51
Read owner() on the three proxies
Reproduce the arXiv:2606.26028 liveness measure on one chain
personas.story: Priya reads the proxies on Ethereum and Base and finds one externally owned account owning all three, with no published holder. She checks the community audit in PR 51, still unmerged, and confirms from the code that a validator can lower a pass and that a requestHash can be claimed first by anyone. Then she samples feedback: most reviewers rate many agents with identical values within minutes, the same pattern arXiv:2606.26028 reported. She writes it up with dates and block numbers, because every one of these facts can change with an upgrade.
